Round-1's blocking gap — the unverified "cache accumulates without eviction/TTL" hop — was closed directly by T4/F34/F35: the TemplateCache counter rises monotonically at ~9,000 entries/hr across 14 samples with evictions=0 everywhere, and resets ONLY at restarts (196,650 → 51,750/49,500/9,000), never at a TTL boundary. The counter↔heap link is corroborated by F36 (old-gen >90% WARNs with 1.6–6.5s full GC pauses in the 85 min before the OOM) and by F15/F16/F37 (flat ~48% through 03-20, linear ramp from ~03-21T01:40, sawtooth resetting on each restart). Temporal order is tight and correct: dep-5402 at 03-21T00:00Z precedes the ramp onset by ~1h40m and the first OOM (03-21T22:59) by ~23h, while the only config change (Kafka retention, 03-23T18:00Z) post-dates both by 1–2 days. Scope is satisfied: the hypothesis explains notification-service's ramp, restarts, lag and email delay, and the co-consumer discriminator was actually run — settlement-service (same shared topic, untouched by dep-5402) is flat on memory (44–56%, no sawtooth), zero restarts, no lag spike at 18:00Z (max 82 msgs), flat CPU, no errors (F26–F32), which is the signature a shared Kafka/replay cause would have produced. Alternatives were tested, not merely dismissed: H5's mechanism was probed and found to have no event-level support (F19/F20/F21/F22/F25 — the complete all-services change feeds contain exactly one kafka row and zero kafka deployments, and no reassignment/rebalance event exists in the window), H3 and H4 are contradicted by lag-follows-restart ordering (F17) and flat throughput/CPU (F18), H6 by the behavioral change in memory (F15/F16), H7 by zero supporting telemetry and the flat co-consumer. Residual uncertainty is real but secondary and non-discriminating: no absolute MB/heap or cache-size metric exists (F33/F38), the per-entry size and configured limit are unknown, and H2 (unbounded userSegment cardinality vs plain no-eviction growth) cannot be separated — but H2 shares H1's origin (dep-5402) and changes only the fix's emphasis, not the responsible change. Likewise the residual "no metric for broker rebalance events" gap cannot revive H5, because the fully-flat, untouched co-consumer on the same topic refutes a shared-side mechanism regardless of feed visibility. critiques.summary: H1 is the best-supported hypothesis: the memory pattern is a multi-day gradual ramp (flat ~48% through 03-20, linear +5-6%/hr from ~03-21T01:40, sawtooth resetting on each restart — F15/F16), which temporally follows dep-5402 (deployed 03-21T00:00Z adding an in-memory TemplateCache keyed by template+locale+userSegment) by ~1h40m and predates the only config change (Kafka retention, 03-23T18:00Z) by two days. Consumer lag spikes occur in the same bucket as each restart rather than leading into it (F17), and throughput/CPU are flat (F18) — together these kill the reporter's replay theory (H3) and the reversed-causality theory (H4). Two of three OOMs predate the maintenance (F13/F14). However, H1's load-bearing hop — that the cache actually accumulates without eviction/TTL — is ASSUMED, with no code inspection, cache-size/cardinality data, or GC data; and the one uncontaminated discriminator (does settlement-service, a co-consumer untouched by dep-5402, show the same sawtooth?) was never queried. H5 (recurring Kafka maintenance/rebalance) is the only surviving alternative naming a different origin and rests solely on precedent with no telemetry, and the Kafka maintenance-event feed was never queried. These gaps are obtainable and could confirm H1 or shift weight to a shared/recurring cause, so I cap confidence at 0.70 rather than accept.

challenges.issue: The pivotal hop — cache entries accumulate without eviction/TTL — is ASSUMED with zero direct evidence: no cache-hit/entry-count metric, no userSegment cardinality data, no dep-5402 code inspection. The entire 'unbounded cache' mechanism rests on inference from a memory ramp shape alone; a leak from any other source (e.g. buffer/logger/ObjectMapper per-request) would produce an identical ramp.

Scope/co-consumer not tested: settlement-service is a co-consumer of the same Kafka topic with no deployments in 10 days (F4). No memory/lag data was pulled for it. If it shows the same sawtooth, H1's single-service cause is contradicted and a shared/recurring origin (H5) rises — this is the single most decisive untested discriminator.

H5 was never actually tested, only dismissed by inference from notification-service's memory shape. It is supported by two same-symptom precedents with operational fixes (HIST-104/HIST-112, both in the same service pair). No Kafka maintenance/reassignment event feed or consumer-group lag series was queried, so 'no maintenance event beyond the config row' is an absence inferred from a data source that was never queried (the Kafka metric-name discovery call was not executed).

Ramp onset attribution: memory data only begins 03-20T00:00Z, so the claim that the baseline was flat and normal before 03-21 is bounded by available data; the report says this is the 'third restart this week' but no pre-03-20 memory/restart data exists to confirm the ramp was truly absent earlier.

H2 is presented as a distinct hypothesis but shares H1's origin (dep-5402); if confirmed it may fold into H1 rather than stand alone. Its key assumption (userSegment cardinality unbounded) is untested and directly addresses H1's load-bearing hop.

critiques.summary: H1 is now well supported and no competitor survives. Round-1's blocking gap — the unverified "cache accumulates without eviction/TTL" hop — was closed directly by T4/F34/F35: the TemplateCache counter rises monotonically at ~9,000 entries/hr across 14 samples with evictions=0 everywhere, and resets ONLY at restarts (196,650 → 51,750/49,500/9,000), never at a TTL boundary. The counter↔heap link is corroborated by F36 (old-gen >90% WARNs with 1.6–6.5s full GC pauses in the 85 min before the OOM) and by F15/F16/F37 (flat ~48% through 03-20, linear ramp from ~03-21T01:40, sawtooth resetting on each restart). Temporal order is tight and correct: dep-5402 at 03-21T00:00Z precedes the ramp onset by ~1h40m and the first OOM (03-21T22:59) by ~23h, while the only config change (Kafka retention, 03-23T18:00Z) post-dates both by 1–2 days. Scope is satisfied: the hypothesis explains notification-service's ramp, restarts, lag and email delay, and the co-consumer discriminator was actually run — settlement-service (same shared topic, untouched by dep-5402) is flat on memory (44–56%, no sawtooth), zero restarts, no lag spike at 18:00Z (max 82 msgs), flat CPU, no errors (F26–F32), which is the signature a shared Kafka/replay cause would have produced. Alternatives were tested, not merely dismissed: H5's mechanism was probed and found to have no event-level support (F19/F20/F21/F22/F25 — the complete all-services change feeds contain exactly one kafka row and zero kafka deployments, and no reassignment/rebalance event exists in the window), H3 and H4 are contradicted by lag-follows-restart ordering (F17) and flat throughput/CPU (F18), H6 by the behavioral change in memory (F15/F16), H7 by zero supporting telemetry and the flat co-consumer. Residual uncertainty is real but secondary and non-discriminating: no absolute MB/heap or cache-size metric exists (F33/F38), the per-entry size and configured limit are unknown, and H2 (unbounded userSegment cardinality vs plain no-eviction growth) cannot be separated — but H2 shares H1's origin (dep-5402) and changes only the fix's emphasis, not the responsible change. Likewise the residual "no metric for broker rebalance events" gap cannot revive H5, because the fully-flat, untouched co-consumer on the same topic refutes a shared-side mechanism regardless of feed visibility. Confidence 0.85 reflects that the causal chain is now evidence-backed at every hop except the unmeasurable absolute-MB arithmetic.

challenges.issue: The quantitative hop "~196,650 entries accounts for the ramp to ~97% of the limit" is unverifiable: no cache-size/RSS/heap metric exists (F33/F38) and the configured memory limit was never retrieved. The ramp↔cache link rests on a log counter overlaid with memory_pct, not a direct heap-vs-cache measurement. This is a real but secondary uncertainty — it does not change which change is responsible.

H2 cannot be separated from H1: there is no per-key cardinality breakdown (template vs locale vs userSegment). If live userSegment is high-cardinality, part of the growth is data-driven. This affects remediation emphasis only; the origin (dep-5402) is identical, so it does not rank a different hypothesis first.

Its load-bearing hop (userSegment values are high-cardinality/unbounded in production) has zero evidence — no cardinality data — and it has no contradicting evidence either. Flagged as an unresolved variant, not a competing origin, and not a blocker for H1.

No direct consumer-group-rebalance / partition-assignment metric exists, so an unlogged broker-side rebalance cannot be excluded from the change feeds alone. However this is mitigated decisively by the co-consumer test (F26–F32): a shared-side event would have hit settlement-service, which is entirely flat. Not blocking.
